system_description.narrative_title: Global bond-market repricing driven by Fed, growth, and oil shocks
system_description.narrative_summary: A broad sell-off in government bonds — led by U.S. Treasuries — is lifting long-term yields and forcing a cross-asset repricing as strong growth data, tightening Fed expectations, rising oil prices and geopolitical risks interact. Treasuries, macro data (jobs/inflation), central bank signaling, commodity shocks and market liquidity form an open system with reinforcing feedbacks: higher yields pressure risk assets and real-economy expectations, which in turn reshape policy expectations and safe‑asset demand. The episode transmits quickly across equities, commodities, FX and credit, while being continuously driven by new data (jobs, oil moves) and policy commentary.
system_description.scope: Government bond markets (U.S. Treasuries and major sovereigns), long-term yields and yield curves, interest-rate expectations, central-bank policy signaling, macro data flows (jobs, inflation), market liquidity and risk-premia, and immediate spillovers to equities, commodities (notably oil), FX and credit markets.
system_description.super_system: Global financial system / global macroeconomic system
adjacent_subsystems: Equity markets and risk asset pricing

variables.name: Long-term sovereign yields
variables.description: The prevailing levels of yields on long-duration government bonds across major maturities.

variables.name: Yield-curve slope
variables.description: The difference between long-term and short-term sovereign yields, capturing term structure shape and steepness.

variables.name: Policy-rate expectations
variables.description: Market-implied expected path of short-term policy rates over the forecast horizon.

variables.name: Central-bank signaling intensity
variables.description: The frequency, clarity and strength of central-bank communications and forward guidance that influence market interpretation of policy stance.

variables.name: Macro data surprise flow
variables.description: The stream and magnitude of incoming macroeconomic releases relative to consensus expectations (positive or negative surprises).

variables.name: Inflation trend
variables.description: The underlying trajectory and persistence of consumer price inflation over time.

variables.name: Economic growth momentum
variables.description: The recent rate of change and acceleration of real economic activity or output growth.

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing market price of crude oil as a representative commodity-price indicator.

variables.name: Market liquidity conditions
variables.description: The ease and cost of executing sizable trades in financial markets without inducing large price moves.

variables.name: Risk premia in risky assets
variables.description: The additional expected return investors demand for holding risky assets instead of safe assets.

variables.name: Safe-asset demand flow
variables.description: Net flows and shifts in investor demand into recognized safe-haven assets over time.

variables.name: Cross-asset spillover intensity
variables.description: The strength and speed with which shocks in one asset class transmit to prices and volatility in other asset classes.

variables.name: Implied volatility
variables.description: Market-implied expected near-term price volatility derived from option prices across asset classes.

variables.name: Credit spread levels
variables.description: Average yield premium of corporate or non-sovereign debt over comparable sovereign yields reflecting credit risk compensation.

variables.name: Foreign-exchange pressure
variables.description: Directional stress, volatility and capital-flow-driven pressure experienced in currency markets.

variables.name: Geopolitical risk tension
variables.description: The intensity and perceived probability of geopolitical developments that could materially disrupt markets and trades.
